You know, I've been thinking about this a lot lately, especially with all the changes in education and technology. (giggles) I mean, I've been teaching for over a decade now, and I've seen so many students come and go. It's hard to say, but I think people are getting smarter in some ways, but dumber in others. (smiling)

On one hand, I think we're getting better at accessing information. With the internet, we have so much knowledge at our fingertips. I mean, I can Google anything I want, and I can learn about it in seconds. That's amazing! But, on the other hand, I think we're also getting lazier. We're relying too much on technology to do the thinking for us. We're not as good at critical thinking and problem-solving as we used to be.

And then there's the whole issue of standardized testing. (sighs) I'm not a fan of it, but it's a reality. I think it's created a culture where students are more focused on memorizing answers rather than truly understanding the material. It's like, they're not learning how to think for themselves, you know? They're just regurgitating what they've memorized.

But, you know, I also think we're getting smarter in other ways. I mean, I've seen so many students who are passionate about social justice and activism. They're thinking critically about the world and trying to make a difference. That's amazing! And with all the advancements in science and technology, we're making progress in so many areas. It's like, we're getting smarter in the sense that we're able to solve problems and make the world a better place.

So, to answer your question, I think people are getting smarter and dumber at the same time. We're getting better at accessing information, but we're also getting lazier and less critical thinkers. But, you know, I'm an optimist. I think we can balance those things out and become even smarter and more compassionate as a society. (smiling)
